decision: Which lead magnet or free tool should we build first, and is a live one bringing in buyers or just emails?
limitations: Idea scores rest on your own answers (appeals only to your buyer, reusable, inputs reveal fit) and your hours estimate. It can't check them or predict whether anyone will use it.
The ten-point scoring, the 80-hour build flag and the verdict cut-offs (40% and 20% fit, 20 emails minimum) are AAJ's rules, not industry benchmarks.
The live readout is only as good as your count of qualified leads. A loose ICP match makes a weak magnet look like a keeper.
Ranking by score per ten build hours favours small builds, so a cheap one-off can outrank a stronger tool. Read the score and the hours together.
review: The marketing lead checks the build estimates include promotion and the follow-up email. The sales lead confirms which emails count as qualified against the ICP before the readout keeps, fixes or retires a magnet.
